main_body: A cradle seen from the side/end: a wooden U-shaped profile with a tall headboard on the left (dark wood interior, white pillow), a low footboard on the right with a blue blanket, rocker feet below. The sides show as a profile silhouette, with only thin rims along the top.
top_band: none: the column at x=8 reads as a dark outline/interior (L=40) over rows 3-8, then a thin 1-row light rim (row 9, L=211), then a wooden side (rows 10-11). No several-row lighter horizontal surface exists.
evidence: The cradle is drawn as a side profile (headboard tall at left, low foot at right, rockers below). The only horizontal 'top' is a 1-row light rim (row 9 L=211) along the cradle side; the interior (pillow, blue blanket) is a vertical-looking cut view rather than a foreshortened surface seen from above. Column x=8 shows 6 rows of dark interior, then a 1-row rim, then 2 rows of wood side, with no top band of 2+ rows and no front-edge/eave construction. This matches the red 'side elevation' failure: a cradle seen end-on with no horizontal surface visible from above.

style.evidence: Measured facts: 19 colours per tile (references 17 and 20), 0% flat-fill coverage, 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is a tinted dark brown that follows the wood. The cradle has about 5 distinct lightness steps (cream rim, wood mid, dark brown, pillow light and shadow greys, blue blanket highlights and shadow), close to the reference's 6. It is small, but its density matches the references and it has no flat fills or sticker-like black outline. It would sit acceptably next to the Beodeul pieces.
